A.rationale: The proposition and conversion sit opposite the sample at desktop and tablet. Mobile follows the same story in one column.
strengths: The filled request button clearly leads the co-located underlined sample link.
The sample becomes product proof in the first desktop and tablet view.
defects: The quantitative proof sits below a large gap on desktop and below the sample on mobile.
A.opportunity: Tighten the separation to the proof strip, especially at desktop.

B.rationale: The italic headline emphasis is legible and the sample separates names, families and prices with type.
strengths: Collection names have a distinctive serif face and price ranges align on the right.
The underlying copy stays comfortably readable at 390px.
defects: The italic phrase starts mid-line at 834px and 390px, weakening the intended phrase break.
The mobile sample family labels wrap in a tight column.
B.opportunity: Tune the headline breaks and use some swatch width to give the scent family more measure.

C.rationale: The cream ground and burgundy sample panel establish strong contrast, with restrained contour lines and a consistent page grid.
strengths: Muted row swatches echo the sample panel motif.
Dividers keep the sample and proof strip orderly.
defects: The generous gap above the desktop proof strip detaches it from the product story.
The final mobile proof metric wraps and looks crowded beside its neighbors.
C.opportunity: Bring the proof strip closer to the hero and balance the mobile cell widths.

D.rationale: The visual language feels premium and the primary brand gesture is the useful comparison itself.
strengths: The burgundy italic, dark sample panel and warm paper feel related.
The sample artwork lends each collection character while the data stays central.
defects: The compact sample looks more like an editorial insert at tablet, where its column spacing is tight.
D.opportunity: Protect the generous desktop sample treatment by giving the tablet panel slightly more width.

E.rationale: The two actions stay in view at every width, and the request state visibly keeps invalid entry in context.
strengths: The invalid mobile form shows a Work email label, entered value, error and submit button together.
The browser trace confirms the valid email confirmation and close action.
defects: The small unframed modal close affordance has low visual weight.
At tablet, the sample is already visible and the post-action capture shows no destination emphasis.
E.opportunity: Give the close action more visible affordance and highlight or focus the sample when it is already in view.

F.rationale: The spacing grid, type roles and table styling carry across screen widths without recorded horizontal overflow.
strengths: Browser evidence exposes row headers scoped to individual collections.
The error state uses the same type and accent system as the landing page.
defects: The contrast audit could not resolve text over the sample pseudo-element.
Keyboard focus restoration after dialog close is unverified.
F.opportunity: Verify contrast over the panel motif and check modal focus restoration.

visual_problems: Large desktop gap before the metrics.
Tablet and mobile scent-family columns wrap tightly.
Mobile proof cells are strained by the wrapped update cadence.
effective_decisions: Sample data acts as the desktop and tablet visual focal point.
Accessible-looking high-contrast primary action and underlined secondary link remain together on mobile.
Serif collection labels and aligned price ranges make the sample easy to scan.
automation_limitations: Automated contrast evaluation is incomplete for the decorated sample. Success and dismissal are verified in the browser log, with no captured success pixels.

A.rationale: The desktop and tablet use the hero for proposition and proof, followed by a well-ordered full-width sample.
strengths: The hero proof strip sits directly below the actions.
At 390px the proposition, actions, proof and all sample rows fit in the supplied initial 844px view.
defects: The large desktop and tablet contour artwork takes the most visually prominent area while the sample sits below.
The desktop sample puts wide gaps between each row’s related values.
A.opportunity: Reduce the hero artwork footprint at wide sizes or pull the sample closer to the action.

B.rationale: Expressive serif headlines, crisp price weights and consistent horizontal rules support reading.
strengths: The regular and italic headline lines stay intact across the three widths.
The mobile table retains readable names and price ranges.
defects: Mobile proof captions and tracked utility labels are small.
The desktop collection header is tiny relative to the rows.
B.opportunity: Increase the sample headers and mobile proof captions by one text step.

C.rationale: Warm off-white and muted olive ground both the illustration and the controls, with an orderly baseline grid.
strengths: The contour art has depth without bright color competing with the CTA.
Hairline dividers and a shaded table header give the sample just enough structure.
defects: At tablet the decorative panel is tall for its information content.
The small dots provide little visual connection between the palette of the chartlike artwork and the sample data.
C.opportunity: Reduce the tablet art height and reuse one contour detail in the sample.

D.rationale: The restrained editorial art direction reads as fragrance research with enough structure for wholesale buyers.
strengths: The abstract contour art evokes discovery without presenting a specific retail product.
The page and mobile dialog share serif headings and warm olive tones.
defects: The art panel and evidence table feel like separate visual systems.
D.opportunity: Echo the contour language within the sample row markers or heading.

E.rationale: Both actions are immediate and all mobile evidence is visible without needing a menu.
strengths: The invalid form has a boxed close action, strong input focus and a nearby red error.
The trace confirms valid submission and closing after confirmation.
defects: At tablet, the already-visible sample receives little feedback when the secondary link is activated.
E.opportunity: Make the sample destination visibly active when the viewport already contains it.

F.rationale: The layouts adapt the same hierarchy without overflow and the error dialog is comfortably spaced.
strengths: The hero art compresses into a shallow mobile panel and all table data remains visible.
Link and button treatments carry through the error state.
defects: The baseline accessibility audit leaves a contrast and an ARIA check incomplete.
Behavior of keyboard focus on dismissal is unverified.
F.opportunity: Confirm the unresolved ARIA and contrast checks and test dialog focus restoration.

visual_problems: Decorative contour panel claims a large share of the desktop and tablet hero.
The desktop row columns are spread far apart.
Small mobile proof captions and tracked table labels limit quick scanning.
effective_decisions: Both actions and all three rows fit in the 390×844 initial view.
Proof sits immediately below the actions.
The error dialog has a clearly bounded close control.
automation_limitations: Automated contrast and ARIA checks are incomplete. Success and dismissal are verified in the browser log, with no captured success pixels.

A.rationale: A sophisticated hero leads to a proof band and a labeled sample section, with the evidence lower in the mobile flow.
strengths: The desktop sample introduction explains the relevance of the table.
Primary and secondary actions sit immediately below the proposition at every width.
defects: The tall mobile bottle panel and sample introduction push the rows below the first 844px viewport.
On desktop, the product-shaped visual rivals the proposition and evidence.
A.opportunity: Shorten the mobile artwork and move the proof strip earlier.

B.rationale: A distinctive, finely drawn serif headline works with straightforward table typography.
strengths: The colored italic phrase creates a clear tonal shift while keeping the headline readable.
Table names are bold and right-aligned prices line up.
defects: The mobile header qualifiers and sample field labels are small and tracked.
The light numerals in the proof band have less presence than nearby display text.
B.opportunity: Lift the size of mobile utility text and add a little weight to the proof figures.

C.rationale: The olive artwork, cream ground and gentle metric band create a cohesive and balanced layout.
strengths: The bottle and contour art share a strong color relationship with the CTA.
Rules and a light proof band separate sections without adding heavy boxes.
defects: The stacked mobile illustration and metrics add a long vertical pause before the sample.
The invalid state puts a red field border directly inside a green focus outline.
C.opportunity: Compress the mobile illustration and unify the invalid focus treatment.

D.rationale: The green and cream identity, bottle rendering and high-contrast serif give the most tangible fragrance cues.
strengths: Art, header mark and italic emphasis feel part of one brand.
The sample introduction frames the content as assortment evidence.
defects: The branded bottle can read as a perfume being sold before the page clarifies that the offering is intelligence.
D.opportunity: Make the hero motif directly evoke the collection index or move part of it into the sample treatment.

E.rationale: The conversion stays above the fold, and the browser trace confirms the request flow and sample availability.
strengths: All collection data remains readable without horizontal page overflow at 390px.
The invalid dialog keeps the required label, inline error and a full-width submit button in view.
defects: On mobile the initial viewport contains the sample title but almost none of its data.
The small unframed close affordance and default un-underlined secondary link are less immediately identifiable.
E.opportunity: Make the sample link visibly link-like by default and reduce the mobile distance to the rows.

F.rationale: The grid, responsive artwork and button treatments stay coherent across layouts and states.
strengths: The two-column sample introduction becomes a readable single-column section at 390px.
The browser run confirms the expected conversion and dismissal behavior.
defects: The audit leaves the arrow and bottle label contrast unevaluated.
Modal keyboard focus is unverified.
F.opportunity: Verify modal keyboard behavior and simplify decoration semantics where the contrast checks are incomplete.

visual_problems: Tall mobile bottle art moves the sample rows below the first screen.
The bottle gives more emphasis to a perfume object than the actual collection evidence.
Red invalid border and green focus outline compete in the request form.
effective_decisions: The custom olive art and high-contrast typography form a cohesive brand.
The muted proof band makes the three proof points recognizable as a group.
The sample keeps all three fields per row at 390px.
automation_limitations: Automated contrast evaluation is incomplete for decorated content. Success and dismissal are verified in the browser log, with no captured success pixels.

pairs.rationale: The burgundy sample puts usable collection evidence next to the proposition at desktop and tablet and reaches the data sooner on mobile. The bottle artwork is polished but occupies the space that could make the offer tangible.

The burgundy data panel is a more distinctive and offer-specific hero treatment, with stronger row identity. The olive treatment gets all the proof into the first mobile viewport and has a clearer dialog close, giving it a real responsive advantage.

The shallow mobile artwork preserves room for both the metrics and all three sample rows in the first view, and the boxed dialog close is clearer. The bottle treatment offers a stronger literal fragrance image but relegates the sample farther down.

A.rationale: A full-width KPI strip leads into the trend, then the departments. The flow remains intact at all widths.
strengths: A large latest-week callout makes the decline apparent before reading the chart.
The chart and all four department rows fit into the initial mobile viewport.
defects: At desktop the first table column is much wider than its content, leaving a long horizontal scan to Sales.
The dark chart surface pulls strongly ahead of the department actions.
A.opportunity: Narrow the first table column and place the core comparison figures closer to department names.

B.rationale: Bold KPIs, visibly link-styled Produce and aligned values create a useful weight hierarchy.
strengths: Gross margin values are easy to compare down the table.
All seven percentage labels and week numbers are present even at 390px.
defects: At mobile the graph axes and per-week values are small and closely spaced.
The headline has tight letter spacing, especially at 390px.
B.opportunity: Increase the mobile chart label space, with a compact value strip if point labeling becomes crowded.

C.rationale: Forest green and lime give the trend a clear focal point, with light surfaces for data entry and scanning.
strengths: Muted pills distinguish all three statuses and include status text.
The trend and latest-week copy stay visibly grouped in both horizontal and stacked layouts.
defects: The graph uses both a tinted area fill and a prominent dark panel.
The large pale region below the desktop table makes the page feel top weighted.
C.opportunity: Reduce the graph fill and use table width more efficiently.

D.rationale: BrightCart gets a recognizable visual identity, while the margin and status indicators are practical for a pricing lead.
strengths: Lime brand mark and chart endpoint feel like a coherent accent.
The separate margin tint and warm Investigate pills support the primary analysis.
defects: The seven-day chart uses a subtle color shift while the summary remains visually unchanged.
D.opportunity: Add a short reporting-period cue to the chart so its seven-day emphasis reads immediately.

E.rationale: Period and status controls remain visible, and Produce reads clearly as an action.
strengths: Mobile preserves both sales and gross margin as well as full status text.
The seven-day and detail captures show the updated values and a reachable close action.
defects: The dialog return is an icon alone rather than a visible action label.
Mobile chart detail requires reading the smallest type in the view.
E.opportunity: Label the detail return and give the seven percentage values a larger predictable text location.

F.rationale: The metric and table roles survive the mobile reflow, and browser evidence confirms the expected update, filter and return behavior.
strengths: Sales becomes secondary text beneath the department on mobile with no reported overflow.
Browser accessibility evidence exposes the values as text spans.
defects: Automated contrast evaluation is incomplete for all seven chart data labels.
The chart’s accessible reading order and detail focus restoration are unverified.
F.opportunity: Manually check chart label contrast and verify the chart text sequence and modal focus cycle.

visual_problems: Small mobile chart text crowds the seven weekly values and axis labels.
Desktop Sales is far from its department names.
The mobile detail visually offers only an X for return.
effective_decisions: Putting mobile Sales below names preserves all values and gives status room.
The latest-week callout states a percentage-point change in words.
The trend and colored status system give the dashboard a recognizable, purposeful identity.
automation_limitations: The axe contrast check is incomplete on chart percentage spans. Screen-reader reading order and modal focus restoration were not exercised in the packet.

A.rationale: The main content has a clear progression from reporting period to KPIs, trend and rows. The shell and tall plot slow the path to departments.
strengths: The gross-margin KPI and trend delta get distinct emphasis.
The detail capture groups the period, margin, supplier-cost note and return in the natural reading order.
defects: The desktop and tablet navigation rail is large for a single Overview item.
The mobile chart and full-width reporting control push most departments below the first screen.
A.opportunity: Cut the single-item navigation footprint and reduce mobile plot height so the first rows appear sooner.

B.rationale: A measured sans-serif hierarchy gives the KPI values prominence and keeps the table compact.
strengths: Desktop and tablet columns align comparable numbers.
The mobile detail labels Last 7 days and Gross margin separately and clearly.
defects: The mobile chart axes are small and only every other historical week is labeled.
Mobile Margin and 7-day status headers sit close together.
B.opportunity: Give the table headers more breathing room and place more trend precision in accessible body-size text.

C.rationale: The white plot, quiet borders and green margin surfaces are restrained. The dark rail has disproportionate visual weight.
strengths: The seven-day plot uses historical dashes, a solid final segment and a light highlight band.
Brief status pills keep warm colors local to exceptions.
defects: A full-height dark rail dominates tablet for one nav item.
Several rounded white cards and individual metric borders create extra chrome on mobile.
C.opportunity: Move the single destination to a compact bar and simplify the mobile KPI container.

D.rationale: The green workspace is appropriate for a commercial dashboard and keeps alert emphasis separate from brand color.
strengths: The seven-day subtitle explains how the latest week relates to the six preceding weeks.
The detail return uses the same accent family as the rest of the app.
defects: The rail and Pricing Workspace eyebrow give this single overview more shell than its content needs.
D.opportunity: Let the margin and department modules define the workspace with a lighter navigation treatment.

E.rationale: The reporting period, explicit status filter and Produce affordance are understandable, with a particularly clear return action.
strengths: The detail has a filled Back to overview button and the required 18.1% margin and Supplier costs.
The filtered background visibly retains Produce and Bakery, and the trace confirms reset.
defects: Weekly values are behind a collapsed disclosure in all supplied captures.
At 390px only the first data row reaches the bottom of the initial viewport.
E.opportunity: Bring the department rows closer to the mobile controls and make the weekly values easier to discover.

F.rationale: The KPI cards, navigation and table adapt to narrow layouts, with clean baseline audit and functional traces.
strengths: The rail converts to a top bar and all four table columns stay reachable without overflow.
The period select and filters tested successfully, and the baseline axe audit had no reported incomplete checks.
defects: The weekly-values disclosure was not expanded in the supplied evidence.
The full-page mobile capture extends below the 844px viewport, and most rows require scrolling.
F.opportunity: Verify the disclosure's text contents and keyboard access and tighten the mobile stacking.

visual_problems: Single-item navigation takes a substantial portion of the tablet and desktop canvas.
Mobile chart height places all but the first department row below the initial viewport.
Most exact weekly values are concealed inside the collapsed chart disclosure.
effective_decisions: Seven-day trend clearly distinguishes prior context and the latest segment.
The explicit, filled return button makes the detail easy to leave.
Mobile retains sales, margin and textual status for every row.
automation_limitations: No supplied capture or test expands Weekly values, so the exact contents and keyboard behavior of that disclosure are unverified.

A.rationale: The trend and department comparisons share the same reading plane at desktop and tablet, below prominent metrics.
strengths: Desktop users can relate the decline to candidate departments without scrolling or switching views.
The mobile view stacks the modules and keeps all four rows and the investigation count within 844px.
defects: The 834px layout leaves both panels comparatively narrow despite ample empty space below.
A.opportunity: Consider stacking the modules slightly earlier so tablet can show the numeric strip with more room.

B.rationale: Bold numerals, margin emphasis in each table row and regular percentage alignment make the important comparisons fast.
strengths: The seven percentages are directly readable in a week/value row across all widths.
The drilldown distinguishes margin, sales and explanatory copy well.
defects: The W1–W7 values look tightly tracked and densely packed at tablet and mobile.
Several mobile table headers are small.
B.opportunity: Increase spacing around the mobile and tablet week values and lift the smallest field labels.

C.rationale: Restrained olive and green tints keep the dashboard quiet while the final point and warning chip carry emphasis.
strengths: The seven-day endpoint treatment combines a highlight band, final segment color and week-cell tint.
Shared card outlines and padding keep the table, trend and detail visually related.
defects: The chart plot leaves a noticeable vertical interval between its subtitle and top gridline.
The mobile plot and details have room for clearer separation among compact week values.
C.opportunity: Reallocate some chart top padding to the numeric strip.

D.rationale: BrightCart has a recognizable compact shell and visual signals that suit a lead scanning for pricing exceptions.
strengths: The investigation count turns raw status labels into a quick action cue.
The detail panel uses the existing KPI language and adds sales alongside margin.
defects: At desktop the compact content cluster leaves the lower half of the canvas largely empty.
D.opportunity: Use a slightly narrower max-width at desktop if needed to give the compact content a more centered, proportional footprint.

E.rationale: Period, status, Produce and return all read as reachable and the browser trace confirms updates and dismissal.
strengths: The latest week remains legible with the earlier six values visible, and the text strip has explicit percent units.
The mobile detail includes a visible Back to overview label and preserves both the selected period and the important figures.
defects: On mobile the period control relies on its displayed value, and the status selector is represented visually by All statuses without a separate visible label.
E.opportunity: Keep an unobtrusive visible Period cue near the mobile control and give the status selector an explicit label if space permits.

F.rationale: The dashboard preserves content and design hierarchy across tested widths and also keeps the chart text visible.
strengths: At 390px the department grid retains names, sales, gross margin and status with no recorded overflow.
The clean baseline axe audit and passes for period, filtering, detail and reset corroborate the visible states.
defects: The packet does not exercise keyboard focus transfer and return in the overlay.
F.opportunity: Verify focus transfer and restoration with the keyboard after filtering and opening the detail.

visual_problems: Week and percentage labels crowd together at 834px and 390px.
The chart reserves generous top padding before the grid.
The mobile period selector has no visible field label.
effective_decisions: Adjacent trend and department cards support one-screen investigation at desktop and tablet.
Full visible numeric week strip and shaded latest-week context preserve the data.
Clearly labeled return and useful margin and sales summary keep the detail purposeful.
automation_limitations: Keyboard focus behavior for the detail is unverified.

pairs.rationale: The side-by-side chart and rows aid desktop scanning, and the compact mobile layout preserves all four rows and the seven exact chart values together. The other layout has a strong return button and trend treatment, with more screen area taken up by its shell and a collapsed weekly-values disclosure.

Both preserve the chart and rows at 390px. The visible numeric value strip, side-by-side wide layout and clearly labeled return give the lighter dashboard an advantage, while the darker chart and large latest callout are strong alternatives for an initial read.

The flatter shell and compact chart allow the four departments and all seven values to stay in the initial mobile viewport. The sidebar dashboard's explicit return and more clearly distinct seven-day chart state are advantages, with more mobile scrolling during the routine overview.

A.rationale: The title, controls and table read in order, but the 390 px hero and toolbar push the table header to about 500 px.
strengths: Price uses strong weight and occupies the first row
The filtered count sits above the retained price and warranty
defects: Mobile reset needs a standalone row
Tablet filtering wraps the toolbar and moves the table down

B.rationale: Dark labels and right-aligned values scan cleanly, with a noticeable hierarchy between model names and values.
strengths: The model headers and their data share one right edge
The price figures are easy to distinguish at all sizes
defects: The tracked uppercase mobile specification header takes nearly all available width
Operating noise wraps at 390 px
B.opportunity: Give the narrow label column slightly more room and use sentence case in the header.

defects: Orbit detail is behind text at 834 px
The mobile controls leave unused space beside Reset

D.rationale: The teal laboratory identity and instrument illustrations give the comparison a clear domain, with a visually heavy landing-style hero.

The domain copy refers directly to fragrance QA
defects: Repeated illustrative forms add limited distinction between models
The hero commands more attention than the comparison

E.rationale: Both interactions passed, and the 390 px table stays scoped with a scroll hint and a separate label column.

defects: Cedar is initially beyond the mobile edge

F.rationale: The captioned table renders consistently and the checked scenarios complete without page errors or page-level overflow.

visual_problems: Tablet orbit overlaps hero text

Visible mobile scroll instruction and separate label column

B.rationale: The serif title and sans interface text establish distinct roles, with aligned numbers and comfortable line spacing.

visual_problems: Desktop page title and detached tracker dominate the compact task

visual_problems: Invalid email is followed by both an error and generic help
The wide desktop success card has little contextual information

effective_decisions: Required markers sit immediately beside both labels
The full-width mobile action is easy to locate

pairs.rationale: The navy shell carries progress and the site into completion and keeps the mobile error compact. The sage version has better required-label proximity and a larger mobile button, but its oversized success view loses request context.

The detached green progress rail stays useful through completion and its confirmation names HVAC and Harbor Annex. The integrated sage version marks required fields more explicitly and gives the reference better typographic emphasis.

The navy flow integrates progress more cleanly with its form, makes FM-2047 quicker to find and places the mobile action higher during validation. The green version supplies a better corrective example and repeats the selected system on success.

A.rationale: The hero conveys shift context and late volume, then a shared header brings the count and filter together. Mobile rows keep all three stop actions comfortably within the initial view.
strengths: Mobile stop and delay share the first line, with the review state and action aligned below.
defects: The mobile filter starts roughly 289 px from the top after stacked shift metrics.
A.opportunity: Compress the phone hero so the control is available sooner.

B.rationale: Strong differentiation between title, stop names and utility labels supports scanning.
strengths: The desktop and tablet ETA column is right-aligned, and the mobile values consistently align to the right edge.
defects: The desktop ETA values are fairly light beside bold delay chips, while the heading tracking is very tight.
B.opportunity: Give ETAs a little more weight and relax the headline tracking.

C.rationale: Deep green bands, pale surface and restrained orange make the exception states salient.
strengths: Muted separators and short orange marks at the left edge distinguish late rows without filling the whole row.
defects: At 834 px the ETA, delay, review and action cells have narrower gutters than the first two columns.
C.opportunity: Redistribute some of the tablet stop and city width to the four right columns.

D.rationale: The compact Harborline mark and green palette carry a recognizable but businesslike dispatch identity.
strengths: The orange late count and row accents reinforce the same operational meaning.
defects: The dark title band carries more visual area than its shift context needs at desktop.
D.opportunity: Reduce the height of the hero while retaining the late count treatment.

E.rationale: The mobile capture shows a filled on switch, two late rows, and Reviewed beside an unchanged 24 min late badge. Desktop reset restores Oak.

defects: The stacked shift counters push the first phone action farther down the page.

F.rationale: All three renderings align without overflow, and the filter and acknowledgement hooks show the expected behavior.
strengths: The same border, badge, and button treatments adapt to the mobile layout with no lost fields.
defects: The 834 px action and review state nearly meet each other on the longest rows.
F.opportunity: Give the review and action cells an explicit minimum gap at the tablet breakpoint.

visual_problems: The dark shift header occupies most of the top 253 px on mobile.

ETA values look subdued beside the delay chips.
effective_decisions: Late counts remain visible above the queue.

A.rationale: The stop and city form a single group, while the column sequence and mobile reading order stay clear.

C.rationale: The blue-gray shell and fine separators are restrained and orderly across widths.

The green screen is more recognizable and puts more of the actionable queue in view on a phone, while the blue screen has an earlier filter and good ETA emphasis.

defects: The digits in the large pale blue step chips are very small and rely on a tiny utility style.

defects: Eight desktop and tablet navigation items had contrast left incomplete by the scan because of a pseudo-element background. Expansion also displaces the mobile outline.

strengths: The equipment button advertises aria-expanded and aria-controls and the selected article exposes aria-current in the browser record.
defects: The contrast scan needs a manual check, and the packet does not demonstrate the supporting destination panels.

visual_problems: The expanded phone tree inserts about 472 px before the article.
Step badges contain small digits relative to their containers.
The Procedures dash repeats the warning color outside the callout.
effective_decisions: A short warning brings the phone outline and first step into view earlier.
The tablet post-action state coordinates the active link, badge and destination heading.
The desktop sidebars and moderate prose measure support long documentation sessions.
automation_limitations: Desktop and tablet axe results left color contrast incomplete for eight sidebar elements because of a pseudo-element. No violations were reported.

pairs.rationale: Both are carefully set manuals. The green version's navigation overlay preserves article position and its cream and green system feels a little more unified. The navy version gets to the steps sooner and has the stronger open-menu and current-target cues.

The serif article, clearly bounded navigation rail and visible tablet target feedback give the green manual stronger hierarchy and orientation. The sans-serif version's explicitly changing mobile close icon is clearer.

The navy version makes the first action easier to reach in the closed phone view and gives the clicked tablet destination much stronger feedback. Its typography and sidebar also feel more specifically designed for a service manual.
